To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the role of the instructor is to facilitate and guide the learner through the learning process.

the instructor must be the guide, not the driver, in the learning process, that the course must be learner driven, not technology driven, and that the course design must be based on an activity cycle, not a content cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of learning environments for the blended classroom, with a focus on the role of the instructor.
how the role of the instructor has changed over time, and the implications of these changes on the design of the learning environment.
the changing role of instructors in the blended learning environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the instructor is not the center of the learning process.
the instructor’s role has changed over time from the Sage on the stage, to the Sage on the slide, to the Guide on the slide, and finally to the Guide on The Side.
the instructor's role in a blended course is to facilitate learning by providing a safe and supportive environment for learners to interact and share knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have moved from the sage on the stage to the guide on the side.
the instructor is a guide, not a sage.
we went from a technology driven, instructor centric, information delivery model, to a learner driven, instructor centred, interaction and collaboration model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design process is an ongoing process that requires a constant evaluation of the learning process, the technology used, the learning environment and the role of the instructor.
we need to move from a focus on technology and the instructor to a focus on the learner.
blended learning is a process, and that it is not possible to design for blended learning without first understanding the instructor role in the process.
